head: claude/mi-182-board-cap-successor
title: MI-182 — retire the capped coordination board, resolve it from one pointer, and make a dead board detectable
body:
## Summary

Issue **#6927** hit GitHub's hard **2500-comment cap** at `2026-09-07T11:28:17Z`. Writes 403; **reads keep succeeding** against a board permanently frozen at that instant — which is the dangerous half, because a read of a frozen board is byte-indistinguishable from a read of a live, quiet one. This re-points every board consumer at a single pointer file, adds a heartbeat so a dead board becomes *detectable* rather than silently indistinguishable from a quiet one, and adds a relay that can provision the next board (no PM-side session can — see Landing).

> ⚠️ **This PR is `landing: hold` (R12).** It edits `board-post.yml` and `session_registry.py`, both in `LANDING_MACHINERY`, and adds a workflow that creates a GitHub issue. A human reads it once, then merges.

### What the work order got wrong, because it changes what had to be built

The brief said `scope-overlap-audit.yml` "reports **0 from a live session** for every PR" and that this "reads as no collision". **Measured: it does not.** `check_scope_overlap.assess` already refused an empty START set as `could_not_check` with an explicit denominator assertion (`scripts/ci/check_scope_overlap.py:434` on `main`), so a fully-frozen board produced a **loud yellow on every PR, not a false green**.

The real defect was narrower and different, and it is why re-pointing alone would not have fixed anything:

1. that yellow is **permanent and indistinguishable from a tooling gap** — the desensitized-alarm class this repo has a P1 rule for; and
2. for the first 24h after the freeze the lookback window still contained **pre-freeze STARTs, graded as if live**.

So the fix had to make the board's **death detectable**, not merely re-point a number.

### The measurement, with its population

- **13 hits across 6 files** — every line matching literal `6927` under `.github/workflows/` and `scripts/` at `main` HEAD. (The brief said 7 files; at this commit it is 6.)
- **#6927 ran 2026-07-19T09:04:33Z → 2026-09-07T11:28:17Z: 2500 comments in 50.1 days = 49.9 comments/day**, over its complete life (population: all 2500 comments). **A fresh board fills in ~7 weeks.**
- Comment #2500 is itself a `merge-claim-audit` post — the brief's claim that the audit's own last post is the ceiling comment is **confirmed**.

### The four constraints

| constraint | how it is met |
|---|---|
| **Don't delete or edit #6927** | Never touched by this PR. `board-rotate.yml` retires it by **title + state only** — `gh issue edit --title` does not send a body, so the 8×-clobbered historical record is not in the payload. |
| **The cap is structural** | Stated with its date: ~7 weeks. The answer is **rotation**, not an accepted limit — the number lives in one file, `board-heartbeat.yml` escalates at `warn_at` (2000, ~10d out) and fails at `rotate_at` (2400, ~2d out), and `board-rotate.yml` makes rotation one JSON edit plus one issue. |
| **A frozen board that reads is the failure to design against** | `board-heartbeat.yml` posts a `HEARTBEAT` every 6h. **A write is the only thing that can distinguish a live board from a frozen one** — no read can, the information is not in the response. Absence of a heartbeat becomes *positive evidence of death*. Second-order: both audits' "a board that is never silent" stops being an empirical assumption about traffic and becomes a **structural invariant**. |
| **Check the 403 relays** | `board-post.yml` **did** need re-pointing (hardcoded `gh issue comment 6927`). `pr-opener.yml` **did not** — it carries no board reference (0 hits). |

### Design notes worth a reviewer's attention

- **`board-post.yml` resolves the pointer from the DEFAULT branch, not the pushed branch.** Its header says the number is hardcoded on purpose so the relay cannot become a general issue-commenting primitive. Reading the pointer off the pushed branch would have handed the caller exactly the control that hardcoding refused them. That property is preserved, not dropped.
- **`board-rotate.yml` exists because the session that notices is the one that cannot fix it.** A PM-side MCP is routinely read-only for issues; measured again here — `issue_write method=create` returned `403 Resource not accessible by integration` (same boundary as `BL-20260901`). This PR was itself opened through `pr-opener.yml` for the same reason.
- **It refuses to create a second live board.** On 2026-08-16, three strays (#9565, #9575, #9590) appeared within 80 minutes and all had to be closed. **Two live boards is strictly worse than one full board** — the sessions split and neither is a coordination board.
- **Honest limit, stated in the workflow header:** nothing watches the watchdog. If `board-heartbeat.yml` itself stops, that is indistinguishable from a dead board. It fails toward "assume dead", which is the safe polarity, and the consumers grade staleness on every PR event so it surfaces there rather than waiting for someone to notice a quiet workflow.
- **Cost against the cap it guards:** 4 beats/day ≈ 200 comments over a ~50-day life, **~8% of the 2500 budget**.

### Duplicate work-object reconciliation

**Kept `WO-20260908-COORDINATION-BOARD-IS-AT-GITHUB-S-2500`** (the object the operator approved, and the one the spawn registry keys on). `WO-20260908-THE-COORDINATION-BOARD-IS-AT-GITHUB-S` is marked `superseded_by` it.

But the keep was the **weaker** of the two on both axes they differed, so **both were taken from the duplicate before it was closed**: `parent_intent` moved `IN-20260903-TRADING-SYSTEM-HEALTH` → `IN-20260901-OPERATING-LAYER` (this is operating-layer machinery, not trading health), and the duplicate's strictly stronger `done_condition` replaced the keep's. Deleting the duplicate and keeping the weaker text would have silently dropped scope.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — no data schema, model boundary, pipeline stage, deployment stage, runtime responsibility, public API, inter-process contract, or configuration shape is touched. Confined to coordination/CI machinery: `.github/workflows/`, `scripts/ci/`, `scripts/ops/session_registry.py`, `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/`. No `src/`, no `config/`, no `deploy/`, no unit file, no order path.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/ci/board_pointer.py --self-test` — refusal paths against planted controls (live / unprovisioned / could_not_check kept distinct; malformed pointers, mis-ordered thresholds and every missing required field refused).
- [x] `scripts/ci/check_board_coherence.py --self-test` — including the two controls that keep it honest: a retired number in a **comment** passes, the same number in **real code** fails.
- [x] `scripts/ci/check_scope_overlap.py --self-test` — **73** planted controls, including new ones proving a `frozen` board turns a would-be `no_overlap` into `could_not_check` *and* suppresses a would-be `overlap`.
- [x] `scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py --base main` → `state=declared_hold`, R8 verified against the diff.
- [x] `check_workflow_catalog.py --all`, `check_document_index.py`, `check_cron_failure_watch.py` — all OK.
- [x] `board-rotate.yml`'s pointer-rewrite jq exercised on both branches (a live slot appends the outgoing board once; an already-retired board is not double-appended).
- [x] `run_guards.py --base main`: **85 pass**. Remaining failures triaged against a clean `main` checkout — 4 are **pre-existing on `main`** (`trainer-capture-watch`, `artifact-validity`, `operator-owed`) or environmental (`layer-guard` / `lint-imports` exit 127, not installed). `cron-failure-watch` **was** caused by this change and is **fixed** here: `board-heartbeat` is cron'd and was watched by nothing, so a scheduled run that died would notify nobody — while every consumer reads a missing heartbeat as proof the board is dead.
- [ ] **`board-coherence` fails until the board is provisioned — this is the forcing function, not a bug.** R2 refuses `board_state: unprovisioned` on `main`, so a half-finished rotation (a board that exists with nothing pointing at it) cannot merge. It clears when `board-rotate.yml` runs and commits the pointer.
- [ ] **The live half of the done-condition: a real posted claim appearing in a scope-overlap-audit verdict.** ⚠️ Not clearable from a harness — a green self-test is a harness result and cannot reach a live board. It is also only reachable **after merge**: `scope-overlap-audit.yml` runs on `pull_request_target`, so both the workflow and the script come from the **base** branch, and this PR's versions do not take effect until they are on `main`.

## Filed for follow-ups

- Deliberately **not** done: no attempt to edit, close, or comment on **#6927** from this session. Closing it is `board-rotate.yml`'s job, in the same run that creates its successor, so the pointer and the retirement can never come apart.
- `capture_idea.py` produced **two** work objects for one operator conversation. The duplicate is closed rather than deleted so that fact stays visible; the capture-side cause is not investigated here.
